caption: Aegis REBOUND: a recovery-aware respiratory digital twin. Team Aegis: Abhishek Bharathi and Aadithya Ram, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Coimbatore.
This silent overview uses captions and actual product captures. Interaction sequences are edited and paced for reading.
The question: when breathing stays raised after everyday activity, which explanation fits the observations?
The product compares ordinary recovery, airway deterioration and sensor drift rather than presenting one unexplained score.
The working prototype combines a personal synthetic EHR with a five-minute wearable and context stream.
Every patient and measurement here is invented. The prototype is for research demonstration and has no clinical validation.
RECAP means Recovery-conditioned Ensemble with Cost-Aware Probing. This screen explains the implemented composition.
The personal record supplies resting heart rate, resting respiratory rate, peak-flow best and history-based priors.
Three explanations times three recovery settings create nine state filters. Each tracks an airway proxy, trend, activity debt and sensor bias.
Kalman updates estimate continuous states. Tempered observation evidence and soft forgetting update the competing model weights.
The planner approximates expected information for peak flow or independent respiratory rate, then subtracts assumed measurement burden.
A wait action is valid. A two-probe daily cap and two-hour cooldown prevent repeated optional measurements.

R-065 at 10:00: before the optional measurement, the airway explanation has 81.2% weight and the low-PEF event estimate is 70.3%.
The planner selects a simulated peak-flow observation because its expected information exceeds its assumed burden.
The optional measurement budget starts at 2 / 2. Clicking the product button reveals an additional synthetic observation.
This is an observation update at the same replay time, so the change can be compared directly with the next capture.
After the actual button interaction, airway weight changes to 97.1%. Ordinary recovery is 1.7%, and sensor drift is 1.3%.
The event estimate changes to 75.6%. Hypothesis weight and event probability answer different questions; they need not change by the same amount.
The remaining budget is 1 / 2. The selected action becomes Wait for passive data, and the optional measurement button is disabled.
The product enforces the cooldown after assimilation. It does not automatically request another measurement to chase certainty.
The Ordinary activity shortcut selects R-064 at 08:00. Here the event estimate is low despite raised breathing during activity.
The planner chooses independent respiratory rate rather than peak flow. Its small positive information-minus-burden score wins.
After the simulated independent-RR measurement, the budget drops from two to one and the product chooses to wait.
The event estimate remains 5.6%. An observation may change the explanation weights only slightly; the demo does not force a dramatic result.
The Ambiguous rise shortcut selects R-066 at 09:00. The three explanations remain close: 25.1%, 36.4% and 38.5%.
The low-PEF event estimate is 7.1%. Uncertainty about the cause does not automatically imply a high event probability.
Peak-flow information is 0.049 nats and assumed burden is 0.035, giving a positive selection score of 0.014.
The optional peak-flow update raises airway weight to 51.1%, with ordinary recovery at 21.3% and sensor drift at 27.6%.
The event estimate changes only to 7.4%. The product retains uncertainty instead of converting the leading explanation into a diagnosis.
The new state is assimilated, the budget is 1 / 2, and cooldown makes waiting the next action.
The Reveal withheld future checkbox is now selected. It adds the held-out synthetic future to the forecast display for retrospective inspection.
The future trace is a comparison overlay. It is not an observation fed into the filter at forecast issue time.
The forecast assumes no further activity and constant current exposure. A mismatch can reveal limitations of those assumptions.
The shaded bands describe mixture moments. Their coverage is uncalibrated, so they are not guaranteed clinical prediction intervals.
The Sensor gap shortcut selects R-066 at 14:30. Last-hour sensor completeness is only 41.7%.
The product replaces explanation weights with Inference withheld and removes the event probability.
The next action becomes Restore sensor data first. The model needs three hours of history, recent HR/RR and at least 75% completeness.
This is a working abstention path: the interface does not display a confident prediction when its required inputs are missing.
The Experiments screen reports a patient-disjoint synthetic benchmark: 48 training, 16 calibration and 24 test patients.
Forecasts issue every thirty minutes for a two-hour target. The endpoint is sustained future low peak flow, including already-low states.
The passive RECAP Brier score is 0.0643. The simpler wearable/context classifier scores about 0.0574, which is better on this benchmark.
The single-recovery ablation also slightly outperforms the recovery bank. These negative comparisons are retained in the product.
All measurement policies share regular four-hourly peak-flow readings. Fixed and adaptive policies have the same cap of two additional probes per day.
Adaptive uses 38 optional probes versus 48 for fixed scheduling. Its Brier score is 0.0593 versus 0.0622 in this synthetic cohort.
The paired patient-bootstrap Brier difference is -0.0028, with a 95% interval from -0.0054 to -0.0002. This is one simulation experiment.
A shifted synthetic cohort gives AUROC 0.906 and Brier 0.075. Changed physiology and noise reduce performance; this is not external clinical validation.
The contribution is this implemented recovery-aware, budgeted hypothesis-bank composition and its reproducible evaluation.
Kalman filtering, Bayesian model averaging, recovery dynamics and information-gain selection already exist. An acronym does not establish scientific novelty.
The planner freezes component risk indices while updating hypothetical weights. It approximates information value rather than exact full-state Bayesian decision theory.
The work needs independent physiological data, calibrated uncertainty, stronger baselines and clinical collaboration before any patient-facing use.
Run START_WINDOWS.bat or python app.py, then open the local address. Explore Recovery twin, Inside RECAP and Experiments; export a case or experiment JSON.
The repository includes implementation, tests, benchmark artifacts, algorithm notes, model/data card, presentation, report and this silent demo. Team Aegis: thank you.
